title.en: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices

value.statement: died aged a little over seventy

units.zh: 劉昫，涿州歸義人也。
units.en: Liu Xu was from Guiyi in Zhuo Prefecture.
units.literal: Liu Xu was a man of Guiyi in Zhuo Prefecture.

units.zh: 昫為人美風儀，與其兄暄、弟暤，皆以好學知名燕、薊之間。
units.en: Xu had fine bearing and deportment, and together with his elder brother Xuan and younger brother Hao, he was known in the Yan and Ji region for love of learning.
units.literal: As a man, Xu had fine bearing and deportment; together with his elder brother Xuan and younger brother Hao, he was known between Yan and Ji for love of learning.

units.zh: 後為定州王處直觀察推官。
units.en: Later he served as investigation judge under Wang Chuzhi of Ding Prefecture.
units.literal: Later he served as Investigation Judge under Wang Chuzhi of Ding Prefecture.

units.zh: 處直為子都所囚，昫兄暄亦為怨家所殺，昫乃避之滄州。
units.en: When Chuzhi was imprisoned by his son Du, and Xu's elder brother Xuan was also killed by an enemy family, Xu took refuge in Cang Prefecture.
units.literal: When Chuzhi was imprisoned by his son Du, and Xu's elder brother Xuan was also killed by an enemy family, Xu accordingly took refuge in Cang Prefecture.

units.zh: 唐莊宗即位，拜昫太常博士，以為翰林學士，明宗時，累遷兵部侍郎居職。
units.en: When Zhuangzong of Tang ascended the throne, Xu was appointed erudite of the Court of Ceremonies and made Hanlin Academician. In Mingzong's reign, he was repeatedly promoted until he held office as Vice Minister of War.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong of Tang ascended the throne, Xu was appointed Erudite of the Court of Ceremonies and made Hanlin Academician; in Mingzong's time, he was repeatedly promoted until he held office as Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 明宗素重昫而愛其風韻，遷端明殿學士。
units.en: Mingzong had always valued Xu and admired his bearing and refinement, and promoted him to Academician of the Duanming Hall.
units.literal: Mingzong had always valued Xu and admired his bearing and refinement, and promoted him to Academician of the Duanming Hall.

units.zh: 長興三年，拜中書侍郎兼刑部尚書、同中書門下平章事，昫詣中興殿門謝，是日大祠不坐，昫入謝端明殿。
units.en: In the third year of Changxing, he was appointed Secretariat Vice Director, concurrently Minister of Justice and Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery. Xu went to the gate of Zhongxing Hall to give thanks, but that day there was a great sacrifice and no audience was held, so he entered and gave thanks at Duanming Hall.
units.literal: In the third year of Changxing, he was appointed Secretariat Vice Director concurrently Minister of Justice and Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery; Xu went to the gate of Zhongxing Hall to give thanks, but that day there was a great sacrifice and no audience was held, so Xu entered and gave thanks at Duanming Hall.

units.zh: 昫自端明殿學士拜相，當時以此為榮。
units.en: Xu was appointed chief minister from the post of Academician of Duanming Hall, and people at the time regarded this as an honor.
units.literal: Xu was appointed chief minister from the post of Academician of Duanming Hall, and people at the time regarded this as an honor.

units.zh: 廢帝入立，遷吏部尚書、門下侍郎，監修國史。
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor entered and was enthroned, Xu was promoted to Minister of Personnel and Chancellery Vice Director, and supervised the compilation of the dynastic history.
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor entered and was enthroned, Xu was promoted to Minister of Personnel and Chancellery Vice Director, and supervised the compilation of the dynastic history.

units.zh: 初，廢帝入，問三司使王玫：「帑廩之數幾何？」
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor first entered and took the throne, he asked Wang Mei, commissioner of the Three Departments: "How large are the treasury and granary holdings?"
units.literal: At the beginning, when the Deposed Emperor entered [the throne], he asked Wang Mei, Commissioner of the Three Departments: "How large are the treasury and granary stores?"

units.zh: 玫言：「其數百萬。」
units.en: Wang Mei said: "Their number is several million."
units.literal: Wang said: "They number in the millions."

units.zh: 及責以賞軍而無十一，廢帝大怒，罷玫，命昫兼判三司。
units.en: When funds were needed to reward the troops and scarcely a tenth of the sum was available, Emperor Fei flew into a rage, removed Wang from office, and ordered Liu Xu to serve concurrently as acting commissioner of the Three Departments.
units.literal: When [the emperor] charged [him] with rewarding the army and there was not one in ten [of what was needed], Emperor Fei was greatly enraged, dismissed Wang, and ordered Xu to take on the additional duty of acting commissioner of the Three Departments.

units.zh: 昫性察，而嫉三司蠹敝尤甚，乃昫計文簿，核其虛實，殘租積負悉蠲除之。
units.en: Liu Xu was sharp by nature and detested the rot in the Three Departments above all else. He personally went through the ledgers, checked fact against fiction, and remitted every outstanding rent and accumulated debt.
units.literal: Xu was by nature observant and especially hated the corruption and waste of the Three Departments; he himself tallied the account books, verified what was false and what real, and completely remitted all residual rents and accumulated arrears.

units.zh: 往時吏幸積年之負蓋而不發，因以把持州縣求賄賂，及昫一切蠲除，民間歡然以為德，而三司吏皆沮怨。
units.en: For years officials had welcomed buried arrears because they could use them to squeeze prefectures and counties for bribes. When Liu Xu wiped the slate clean in one stroke, the common people hailed it as a blessing, but every clerk in the Three Departments seethed with resentment.
units.literal: In former times officials were glad that accumulated arrears of many years were covered and not exposed, and thereby used them to control prefectures and counties and seek bribes; when Xu remitted everything at once, the people gladly regarded it as a virtue, while all the Three Departments clerks were resentful and bitter.

units.zh: 先是，馮道與昫為姻家而同為相，道罷，李愚代之。
units.en: Earlier Feng Dao and Liu Xu had been in-laws and served together as chancellors. When Feng left office, Li Yu took his place.
units.literal: Earlier, Feng Dao and Xu were related by marriage and served together as chancellors; when Feng was dismissed, Li Yu replaced him.

units.zh: 愚素惡道為人，凡事有稽失者，必指以誚昫曰：「此公親家翁所為也！」
units.en: Yu had long despised Feng Dao's character. Whenever something was delayed or mishandled, he would point to it and taunt Liu Xu: "This is the doing of your father-in-law!"
units.literal: Yu had always disliked Feng's conduct as a man; whenever anything had a lapse or error, he would point at it and mock Xu, saying, "This is what your father-in-law did!

units.zh: 昫性少容恕，而愚特剛介，遂相詆詬。
units.en: Liu Xu was not much given to forbearance, and Yu was uncommonly stiff and upright, so the two men fell to trading insults.
units.literal: Xu was by nature not very forgiving, while Yu was especially rigid and principled, so they came to revile each other.

units.zh: 相府史吏惡此兩人剛直，因共揚言，其事聞，廢帝並罷之，以昫為右僕射。
units.en: The chancellery clerks loathed both men's inflexibility and spread word of their quarrel. When Emperor Fei heard of it, he dismissed them both and made Liu Xu right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.
units.literal: The staff clerks of the chancellery hated these two men's rigidity; they therefore spread rumors together. When the matter was heard, Emperor Fei dismissed them both and appointed Xu Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 是時，三司諸吏提印聚立月華門外，聞宣麻罷昫相，皆歡呼相賀曰：「自此我曹快活矣！」
units.en: The Three Departments clerks had clustered outside the Moon Flower Gate with their seals in hand. When they heard the edict removing Liu Xu from the chancellorship, they burst into cheers: "Now we can live easy at last!"
units.literal: At that time the various clerks of the Three Departments gathered outside the Moon Flower Gate holding their seals; hearing the proclamation that Xu was removed from the chancellorship, they all cheered and congratulated one another, saying, "From now on we fellows will be able to enjoy ourselves!"

units.zh: 昫在相位，不習典故。
units.en: As chancellor, Liu Xu was unfamiliar with court precedent.
units.literal: While Xu was in the chancellorship, he was not versed in precedent and regulations.

units.zh: 初，明宗崩，太常卿崔居儉以故事當為禮儀使，居儉辭以祖諱蠡。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong died, Cui Jujian, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, should by precedent have become commissioner of rites, but he declined because his grandfather's taboo name was Li.
units.literal: At the beginning, when Emperor Mingzong died, the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Jujian, according to precedent, ought to have become Commissioner of Rites; Jujian declined on the ground that his grandfather's taboo name was Li.

units.zh: 馮道改居儉秘書監，居儉怏怏失職。
units.en: Feng Dao reassigned Jujian to director of the Palace Library, and Jujian took the demotion bitterly.
units.literal: Feng Dao changed Jujian to Director of the Palace Library; Jujian was discontented at losing his post.

units.zh: 中書舍人李詳為居儉誥詞，有「聞名心懼」之語，昫輒易曰「有恥且格」。
units.en: Li Xiang, a secretariat drafter, wrote Jujian's appointment edict with the phrase "hearing the name, one's heart quails." Liu Xu at once changed it to "having shame, and moreover reforming oneself."
units.literal: The Secretariat Drafter Li Xiang wrote the appointment text for Jujian with the phrase "hearing the name, the heart is afraid"; Xu immediately changed it to "having shame and moreover correcting [oneself]."

units.zh: 居儉訴曰：「名諱有令式，予何罪也？」
units.en: Jujian protested: "Taboo names are governed by statute. What offense have I committed?"
units.literal: Jujian complained, saying, "Taboo names have regulations and forms—what crime have I committed?

units.zh: 當時聞者皆傳以為笑。
units.en: Everyone who heard the story passed it around as a joke.
units.literal: Those who heard of it at the time all spread it about as a laughing matter.

units.zh: 及為僕射，入朝遇雨，移班廊下，御史臺吏引僕射立中丞御史下，昫詰吏以故事，自宰相至臺省皆不能知。
units.en: After he became vice director, rain fell during court and the officials moved under the corridor. A censorate clerk placed the vice director below the censors and assistant censors. Liu Xu asked what precedent supported this, but neither the chancellors nor anyone in the censorate or secretariat could say.
units.literal: When he became Vice Director, on entering court he encountered rain and the ranks moved under the corridor; a censorate clerk led the Vice Director to stand below the censors and assistant censors. Xu questioned the clerk about precedent, but from the chancellor down to the censorate and secretariat none could know.

units.zh: 是時，馮道罷相為司空。
units.en: By then Feng Dao had left the chancellorship and been made minister of works.
units.literal: At that time Feng Dao had left the chancellorship and become Minister of Works.

units.zh: 自隋、唐以來，三公無職事，不特置，及道為司空，問有司班次，亦皆不能知，由是不入朝堂，俟臺官、兩省入而後入，宰相出則隨而出。
units.en: Since Sui and Tang times the Three Dukes had held no active duties and were not specially appointed. When Feng Dao became Sikong, Minister of Works, and asked the proper offices about the order of court ranking, they also could not tell him. He therefore did not enter the audience hall, but waited until the censorate officials and the two departments had entered and then went in; when the chancellors came out, he followed them out.
units.literal: From Sui and Tang onward the Three Dukes had no duties and were not specially appointed; when Dao became Minister of Works and asked the relevant offices about order of precedence, they too could not know. Thereupon he did not enter the main hall of court but waited until the censorate officials and the two secretariats had entered before entering himself, and when the chancellor left he followed out.

units.zh: 至句為僕射，自以由宰相罷，與道同，乃隨道出入，有司不能彈正，而議者多竊笑之。
units.en: When Liu Xu became vice director, he too had just left the chancellorship and thought himself in the same position as Feng, so he followed Feng in and out of court. The proper offices could not correct the practice, and many observers quietly ridiculed them.
units.literal: When Xu became Vice Director, he considered that he too had been dismissed from the chancellorship and was in the same situation as Dao, so he followed Dao in and out; the relevant offices could not correct this, and many in discussion secretly laughed at it.

units.zh: 晉高祖時，張從賓反，殺皇子重乂於洛陽，乃以昫為東都留守，判鹽鐵。
units.en: Under Gaozu of Later Jin, Zhang Congbin rebelled and killed the prince Chongyi at Luoyang. Liu Xu was appointed regent of the eastern capital with concurrent charge of the salt and iron monopoly.
units.literal: In the time of Gaozu of Jin, Zhang Congbin rebelled and killed the imperial prince Chongyi at Luoyang; [the court] then appointed Xu Eastern Capital Regent with concurrent charge of salt and iron.

units.zh: 開運中，拜司空、同中書門下平章事，復判三司。
units.en: During the Kaiyun period he was made minister of works and grand councilor, and again assumed charge of the Three Departments.
units.literal: In the Kaiyun era he was appointed Minister of Works and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and again took charge of the Three Departments.

units.zh: 契丹犯京師，昫以目疾罷為太保，是歲卒，年六十。
units.en: When the Khitans attacked the capital, Liu Xu was relieved on account of eye trouble and made grand guardian. He died that same year at the age of sixty.
units.literal: When the Khitan invaded the capital, Xu was removed on account of eye disease and made Grand Guardian; that year he died, aged sixty.

units.zh: 盧文紀
units.en: Lu Wenji
units.literal: Lu Wenji

units.zh: 盧文紀，字子持，其祖簡求，為唐太原節度使，父嗣業，官至右補闕。
units.en: Lu Wenji, courtesy name Zichi, came from a line whose grandfather Jianqiu had been Tang military commissioner of Taiyuan and whose father Siye had risen to right remonstrator.
units.literal: Lu Wenji, courtesy name Zichi—his grandfather Jianqiu was Tang military commissioner of Taiyuan; his father Siye reached the office of Right Remonstrator.

units.zh: 文紀舉進士，事梁為刑部侍郎、集賢殿學士。
units.en: Wenji passed the jinshi examination and served Later Liang as vice minister of justice and academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.
units.literal: Wenji passed the jinshi examination and served Liang as Vice Minister of Justice and Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.

units.zh: 唐明宗時，為御史中丞。
units.en: Under Tang Emperor Mingzong he served as censor-in-chief.
units.literal: In the time of Tang Emperor Mingzong he was Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 初上事，百官臺參，吏白諸道進奏官賀，文紀問：「當如何？」
units.en: On his first day in office, the officials attended the censorate audience. A clerk reported that the memorial-presenting officers from the circuits had come to offer congratulations. Wenji asked: "How should this be handled?"
units.literal: When he first took office, the hundred officials attended court at the censorate; a clerk announced that the memorial-presenting officials of the various circuits had come to congratulate. Wenji asked, "What ought to be done?

units.zh: 吏對曰：「朝廷在長安時，進奏官見大夫、中丞如胥史。
units.en: The clerk replied: "When the court was at Chang'an, memorial-presenting officers saw grandees and censors as if they were clerks and scribes.
units.literal: The clerk replied, "When the court was at Chang'an, memorial-presenting officials met grandees and censors-in-chief like clerks and attendants.

units.zh: 自唐衰，天子微弱，諸侯強盛，貢奉不至，朝廷姑息方鎮，假借邸吏，大夫、中丞上事，進奏官至客次通名，勞以茶酒而不相見，相傳以為故事。」
units.en: After Tang declined, the Son of Heaven was weak and the regional lords were strong. Tribute and offerings no longer arrived, and the court indulged the military governors and gave latitude to hostel clerks. When a grandee or censor first took office, the memorial-presenting officers came to the guest quarters, announced their names, were comforted with tea and wine, and did not meet him in person. This was handed down as precedent."
units.literal: Since Tang's decline the Son of Heaven had been weak, the feudal lords strong, and tribute did not arrive; the court indulged the military commissioners and deferred to the hostel clerks. When grand masters and censors-in-chief took office, memorial-presenting officials would announce their names in the reception room, be offered tea and wine in courtesy, and not be received in audience—this was transmitted and regarded as established practice."

units.zh: 文紀曰：「吾雖德薄，敢隳舊制？」
units.en: Wenji said, "However slight my standing, how dare I tear down the old order?"
units.literal: Wenji said, "Although my virtue is slight, how dare I destroy the old system?"

units.zh: 因遣吏諭之。
units.en: He sent a clerk to instruct them accordingly.
units.literal: He thereupon sent a clerk to instruct them.

units.zh: 進奏官奮臂喧然欲去，不得已入見，文紀據床端笏，臺吏通名贊拜，既出，恚怒不自勝，訴於樞密使安重誨。
units.en: The memorial-presenting officers erupted in protest and tried to leave, but had no choice except to come in. Wenji sat formal on the couch with his tablet raised while censorate clerks announced names and directed the bows. Once outside they were beside themselves with fury and appealed to the commissioner of military affairs, An Chonghui.
units.literal: The memorial-presenting officials waved their arms and clamored, wanting to leave; having no choice they entered for an audience. Wenji sat upright on the couch holding his tablet; censorate clerks announced names and led the bows. After they left, unable to contain their rage, they complained to the Commissioner of Military Affairs An Chonghui.

units.zh: 重誨曰：「吾不知故事，可上訴於朝。」
units.en: Chonghui told them, "I do not know the precedent here. You may appeal to the court."
units.literal: Chonghui said, "I do not know the established practice; you may appeal to the court above.

units.zh: 即相率詣閣門求見以壯訴。
units.en: They went in a body to the Gate of Memorials to demand an audience and press their case.
units.literal: They thereupon went together to the Gate of Memorials to seek an audience and press their complaint.

units.zh: 明宗問宰相趙鳳：「進奏吏比外何官？」
units.en: Mingzong asked Chancellor Zhao Feng: "Compared with outside officials, what office are memorial-presenting clerks equivalent to?"
units.literal: Mingzong asked the chancellor Zhao Feng, "Compared with outside officials, what rank are memorial-presenting clerks?

units.zh: 鳳曰：「州縣發遞知後之流也。」
units.en: Feng said: "They are the sort of men who manage dispatches and post-delivery in prefectures and counties."
units.literal: Feng said, "They are of the sort of prefectural and county dispatch runners and post-station supervisors."

units.zh: 明宗怒曰：「乃吏卒爾，安得慢吾法官！」
units.en: Mingzong flared up: "They are nothing but clerks and runners. How dare they slight my judicial officers!"
units.literal: Mingzong said angrily, "They are mere clerk-soldiers—how dare they slight my judicial officers!"

units.zh: 皆杖而遣之。
units.en: He had them all flogged and sent away.
units.literal: All were beaten with the staff and dismissed.

units.zh: 文紀又請悉復中外官校考法，將相天子自書之，詔雖施行，而官卒不考。
units.en: Wenji also asked that the annual evaluation system for all officials be fully restored, with the emperor personally writing the reviews of generals and ministers. An edict was issued, but in the end the evaluations were never carried out.
units.literal: Wenji also requested fully restoring the method of annual evaluation for inside and outside officials, with generals and ministers written up by the Son of Heaven himself; although an edict was issued and put into effect, in the end officials were not evaluated.

units.zh: 歲餘，遷工部尚書。
units.en: A little over a year later he was promoted to minister of works.
units.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Minister of Works.

units.zh: 文紀素與宰相崔協有隙，協除工部郎中於鄴，文紀以鄴與其父名同音，大怒，鄴赴省參上，文紀不見之，因請連假。
units.en: Wenji had long been at odds with Chancellor Cui Xie. When Xie appointed Yu Ye as a director in the Ministry of Works, Wenji flew into a rage because Ye was homophonous with his father's name. When Ye came to the ministry for his induction audience, Wenji refused to receive him and took an extended leave.
units.literal: Wenji had long had a rift with Chancellor Cui Xie; Xie appointed Yu Ye as a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works. Wenji, because Ye was homophonous with his father's name, was greatly enraged. When Ye came to the ministry to pay his respects on taking office, Wenji would not see him and thereupon requested continuous leave.

units.zh: 已而鄴奉使未行，文紀即出視事，鄴因醉忿自經死，文紀坐貶石州司馬。
units.en: Before Ye could depart on a mission he was assigned, Wenji returned to his desk. Ye, drunk and enraged, hanged himself. Wenji was demoted to military adjutant of Shizhou.
units.literal: Before long Ye was to go on a mission but had not yet departed; Wenji immediately came out to attend to business. Ye, in drunken rage, hanged himself; Wenji was demoted to military adjutant of Shizhou on account of it.

units.zh: 久之，為秘書監、太常卿。
units.en: After a long interval he was made director of the Palace Library and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: After a long while he became Director of the Palace Library and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 奉使於蜀，過鳳翔。
units.en: On a mission to Shu he passed through Fengxiang.
units.literal: On a mission to Shu he passed through Fengxiang.

units.zh: 時廢帝為鳳翔節度使，文紀為人形貌魁偉、語音瑯然，廢帝奇之。
units.en: Emperor Fei was then military commissioner of Fengxiang. Wenji was tall and imposing, with a ringing voice, and the future emperor was struck by him.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Fei was military commissioner of Fengxiang. Wenji was a man of imposing stature and clear, resonant speech; Emperor Fei marveled at him.

units.zh: 後廢帝入立，欲擇宰相，問於左右，左右皆言：「文紀及姚顗有人望。」
units.en: After Emperor Fei entered and took the throne, he wanted to choose a chancellor and asked his attendants. The attendants all said: "Wenji and Yao Yi have public esteem."
units.literal: Later, when Emperor Fei took the throne, he wished to choose a chancellor and asked those around him; they all said, "Wenji and Yao Yi enjoy public esteem.

units.zh: 廢帝因悉書清望官姓名內琉璃瓶中，夜焚香祝天，以箸挾之，首得文紀，欣然相之，乃拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: The emperor wrote the names of every eminent official into a glass jar, burned incense that night and prayed to Heaven, then drew a name with chopsticks. Wenji's came out first. Delighted, he appointed him vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor.
units.literal: Emperor Fei thereupon wrote the names of all officials of clear reputation inside a glass bottle, burned incense at night and prayed to Heaven, and drew one with chopsticks; Wenji came out first. Delighted, he made him chancellor, appointing him Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 是時，天下多事，廢帝數以責文紀。
units.en: The realm was in turmoil, and Emperor Fei blamed Wenji again and again.
units.literal: At that time the realm had many troubles; Emperor Fei repeatedly blamed Wenji for them.

units.zh: 文紀因請罷五日起居，復唐故事，開延英，冀得從容奏議天下事。
units.en: Wenji asked to abolish the five-day audience, restore Tang practice, and open the Yanying Hall so he could discuss state affairs at length.
units.literal: Wenji thereupon requested abolishing the five-day court audience, restoring Tang precedent, and opening the Yanying Hall, hoping thereby to discuss the affairs of the realm at leisure.

units.zh: 廢帝以謂五日起居，明宗所以見群臣也，不可罷，而便殿論事，可以從容，何必延英。
units.en: Emperor Fei replied that the five-day audience was how Mingzong had met his ministers and could not be dropped, and that the side hall was already leisurely enough—there was no need for the Yanying Hall.
units.literal: Emperor Fei held that the five-day audience was how Emperor Mingzong had seen his ministers and could not be abolished, while discussing affairs in the side hall could be leisurely—why must it be the Yanying Hall?

units.zh: 因詔宰相有事，不以時詣閣門請對。
units.en: He ordered that chancellors with business should not seek audiences at the Gate of Memorials at improper hours.
units.literal: He therefore issued an edict that when chancellors had business, they should not at untimely hours go to the Gate of Memorials to request an audience.

units.zh: 晉高祖起太原，廢帝北征，過拜徽陵，休仗舍，顧文紀曰：「吾自鳳翔識卿，不以常人為待，自卿為相，詢於輿議，皆云可致太平，今日使吾至此，卿宜如何？」
units.en: When Gaozu of Jin rose in Taiyuan, Emperor Fei marched north. Passing by to pay respects at Huiling, he rested in the guard quarters and turned to Wenji: "I knew you from Fengxiang and did not treat you as an ordinary man. Since you became chancellor, I inquired among public opinion, and all said you could bring about great peace. Today you have brought me to this point; what should you do?"
units.literal: When Gaozu of Jin rose at Taiyuan, Emperor Fei marched north on campaign; passing to pay respects at the Huiling tomb, he rested at the guard barracks and turned to Wenji, saying, "I knew you since Fengxiang and did not treat you as an ordinary man. Since you became chancellor, inquiry in public discussion all said you could bring about peace. Today you have brought me to this—what ought you to do?

units.zh: 文紀皇恐謝罪。
units.en: Wenji fell to his knees in terror and begged forgiveness.
units.literal: Wenji, in terror, apologized for his offense.

units.zh: 廢帝至河陽，文紀勸帝扼橋自守，不聽。
units.en: At Heyang, Wenji urged the emperor to hold the bridge and stand his ground, but the emperor would not listen.
units.literal: When Emperor Fei reached Heyang, Wenji urged the emperor to hold the bridge and defend himself; he would not listen.

units.zh: 晉高祖入立，罷為吏部尚書，累遷太子太師，致仕。
units.en: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, Wenji was removed to minister of personnel, later promoted to grand preceptor of the heir apparent, and finally retired.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, [Wenji] was removed and made Minister of Personnel; he was promoted in succession to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.

units.zh: 周太祖入立，即拜司空於家。
units.en: When Taizu of Later Zhou took the throne, he appointed Wenji minister of works at his home.
units.literal: When Taizu of Zhou took the throne, he immediately appointed him Minister of Works at his home.

units.zh: 卒，年七十六，贈司徒。
units.en: He died at seventy-six and was posthumously made minister of education.
units.literal: He died, aged seventy-six, and was posthumously given the title of Minister of Education.

units.zh: 馬胤孫
units.en: Ma Yinxun
units.literal: Ma Yinxun

units.zh: 馬胤孫，字慶先，棣州商河人也。
units.en: Ma Yinxun, courtesy name Qingxian, was a native of Shanghe in Dizhou.
units.literal: Ma Yinxun, courtesy name Qingxian, was a native of Shanghe in Dizhou.

units.zh: 為人懦暗，少好學，學韓愈為文章。
units.en: He was timid and slow-witted, but studious from youth and wrote in imitation of Han Yu.
units.literal: As a man he was timid and dull; in youth he loved learning and studied Han Yu's style in composition.

units.zh: 舉進士，為唐潞王從珂河中觀察支使。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination and became staff officer to Li Congke, the Prince of Lu, in his Hezhong observation mission.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became staff officer to Tang's Prince of Lu, Li Congke, in his Hezhong observation mission.

units.zh: 從珂為楊彥溫所逐，罷居於京師裏第，胤孫從而不去。
units.en: When Congke was driven out by Yang Yanwen and sent to live in his mansion in the capital, Yinxun stayed with him and would not leave.
units.literal: Congke was driven out by Yang Yanwen and dismissed to reside in his mansion in the capital; Yinxun followed and did not leave.

units.zh: 從珂為京兆尹，徙鎮鳳翔，胤孫常從之，以為觀察判官。
units.en: When Congke became metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and was transferred to Fengxiang, Yinxun went with him and was made administrative aide of the observation mission.
units.literal: When Congke became Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and was transferred to garrison Fengxiang, Yinxun often followed him and was made administrative aide of the observation mission.

units.zh: 潞王將舉兵反，與將吏韓昭胤等謀議已定，召胤孫告之曰：「受命移鎮，路出京師，何向為便？」
units.en: When the Prince of Lu was about to raise troops in rebellion, he had already settled plans with Han Zhaoyin and the other officers. He summoned Yinxun and told him: "I have received orders to move my command, and the route goes through the capital. Which direction would be best?"
units.literal: When the Prince of Lu was about to raise troops in rebellion, having already settled plans with his generals and officials Han Zhaoyin and others, he summoned Yinxun and told him, "Having received orders to transfer my garrison, my route passes through the capital—which direction is convenient?

units.zh: 胤孫曰：「君命召，不俟駕。
units.en: Yinxun quoted the classic: "When the ruler summons, one does not wait even to harness the carriage.
units.literal: Yinxun said, "When the ruler's command summons, one does not wait for the carriage to be yoked.

units.zh: 今大王為國宗屬，而先帝新棄天下，臨喪赴鎮，臣子之忠也。」
units.en: Your Highness is a member of the imperial clan, and the late emperor has only just died. To proceed to your post while observing mourning is the duty of a loyal subject."
units.literal: Now Your Highness is a clansman of the state, and the late emperor has newly left the world; to go to one's post while attending the mourning is a subject's loyalty."

units.zh: 左右皆笑其愚，然從珂心獨重之。
units.en: Those around the prince laughed at his naivety, but Congke alone came to value him.
units.literal: Those around him all laughed at his foolishness, yet Congke in his heart alone valued him.

units.zh: 廢帝入立，以為戶部郎中、翰林學士。
units.en: When Emperor Fei took the throne, Yinxun was made bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and Hanlin academician.
units.literal: When Emperor Fei took the throne, [Yinxun] was made Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Hanlin Academician.

units.zh: 久之，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: In time he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor.
units.literal: After a long while he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 胤孫不通世務，故事多壅塞。
units.en: Yinxun understood nothing of practical affairs, and court precedent piled up unresolved.
units.literal: Yinxun did not understand worldly affairs; many established practices were blocked up.

units.zh: 是時，馮道罷匡國軍節度使，拜司空。
units.en: At that time Feng Dao left the Kuangguo army command and was appointed minister of works.
units.literal: At that time Feng Dao left the post of military commissioner of the Kuangguo Army and was appointed Minister of Works.

units.zh: 司空自唐已來無特拜者，有司不知故事，朝廷議者紛然，或曰司空三公，宰相職也，當參與大政，而宰相盧文紀獨以謂司空之職，祭祀掃除而已。
units.en: Since Tang times no one had been specially appointed Sikong, Minister of Works, and the proper offices did not know the precedent. Debate at court was confused. Some said that the Sikong, as one of the Three Dukes, was a chancellor-level office and should take part in great affairs of state, while Chancellor Lu Wenji alone held that the duty of the Sikong was merely sweeping for sacrifices.
units.literal: Since Tang there had been no special appointment as Minister of Works; the relevant offices did not know the precedent. Court discussants were divided: some said the Minister of Works was one of the Three Dukes and a chancellor's duty, and ought to participate in great affairs; the chancellor Lu Wenji alone held that the duty of Minister of Works was merely sweeping for sacrifices.

units.zh: 胤孫皆不能決。
units.en: Yinxun could decide none of it.
units.literal: Yinxun could decide none of these matters.

units.zh: 時劉句亦罷相為僕射，右散騎常侍孔昭序建言：「常侍班當在僕射前。」
units.en: Liu Xu had also left the chancellorship and become vice director. Kong Zhaoxu, right regular attendant, proposed: "The regular attendant's rank should stand ahead of the vice director."
units.literal: At that time Liu Xu also had left the chancellorship and become Vice Director; the Right Regular Attendant Kong Zhaoxu submitted a proposal: "The regular attendant's rank ought to be before the Vice Director.

units.zh: 胤孫責御史臺檢例，臺言：「故事無所見，據今南北班位，常侍在前。」
units.en: Yinxun ordered the censorate to search the precedents. The censorate reported: "No precedent can be found. According to the current north and south court ranks, the regular attendant stands in front."
units.literal: Yinxun charged the censorate to search precedents; the censorate said, "No precedent is found; according to present north-south court positions, the regular attendant is in front."

units.zh: 胤孫即判臺狀施行，劉句大怒。
units.en: Yinxun approved the censorate report at once. Liu Xu was furious.
units.literal: Yinxun immediately approved the censorate's report for implementation; Liu Xu was greatly enraged.

units.zh: 崔居儉揚言於朝曰：「孔昭序解語，是朝廷無解語人也！
units.en: Cui Jujian declared in open court, "So Kong Zhaoxu understands language—does that mean the court has no one who does?
units.literal: Cui Jujian proclaimed in court, "Kong Zhaoxu understands language—does that mean the court has no one who understands language!

units.zh: 且僕射師長百寮，中丞、大夫就班修敬，而常侍在南宮六卿之下，況僕射乎？
units.en: Besides, the vice director is senior to the whole bureaucracy. Censors-in-chief and grandees take their places before him in respect. Regular attendants rank below the six ministers of the southern palace—how much more should they rank below a vice director?
units.literal: Moreover the Vice Director is teacher and elder to the hundred officials; censors-in-chief and grandees come to their ranks to show respect, while the regular attendant is below the six ministers of the Southern Palace—how much more so the Vice Director?

units.zh: 昭序癡兒，豈識事體？」
units.en: Zhaoxu is a fool. How could he understand the substance of the matter?"
units.literal: Zhaoxu is a foolish child—how could he understand how things ought to be?

units.zh: 朝士聞居儉言，流議稍息。
units.en: When courtiers heard Jujian's outburst, the controversy gradually died down.
units.literal: When court gentlemen heard Jujian's words, the floating discussion gradually subsided.

units.zh: 胤孫臨事多不能決，當時號為「三不開」，謂其不開口以論議，不開印以行事，不開門以延士大夫也。
units.en: Yinxun could rarely decide anything. People called him "the Three Not Opens": he would not open his mouth to debate policy, open his seal to transact business, or open his door to receive gentlemen of the court.
units.literal: Yinxun in facing affairs often could not decide; at the time he was nicknamed "the Three Not Opens," meaning he did not open his mouth to discuss policy, did not open his seal to conduct business, and did not open his door to receive scholar-officials.

units.zh: 晉兵起太原，廢帝至河陽，是時勢已危迫，胤孫自洛來朝行在，人皆冀其有所建言，胤孫獻綾三百匹而已。
units.en: When Jin forces rose in Taiyuan and Emperor Fei reached Heyang, the situation was desperate. Yinxun came from Luoyang to the traveling court. Everyone hoped for counsel; he brought only three hundred bolts of silk.
units.literal: When Jin troops rose at Taiyuan and Emperor Fei reached Heyang, the situation was already critically urgent. Yinxun came from Luoyang to attend the traveling court; everyone hoped he would offer some counsel, but Yinxun presented only three hundred bolts of thin silk.

units.zh: 晉高祖入立，罷歸田里。
units.en: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, Yinxun was dismissed and sent home.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, [Yinxun] was removed and returned to his fields and villages.

units.zh: 胤孫既學韓愈為文，故多斥浮屠氏之說，及罷歸，乃反學佛，撰《法喜集》、《佛國記》行於世。
units.en: Having written in Han Yu's manner, Yinxun had often attacked Buddhism. After his dismissal he took up Buddhism instead and wrote the Collections of Dharma Joy and Record of the Buddha Land, which circulated widely.
units.literal: Yinxun had studied Han Yu in composition and therefore often denounced Buddhist doctrine; when he was dismissed and returned home, he turned instead to studying Buddhism and compiled the Collections of Dharma Joy and Record of the Buddha Land, which circulated in the world.

units.zh: 時人誚之曰：「佞清泰不徹，乃來佞佛。」
units.en: People of the time mocked him, saying: "He did not finish fawning on Qingtai, and now he has come to fawn on the Buddha."
units.literal: People of the time mocked him, saying, "Flattering Qingtai was not thorough enough—so now he comes to flatter the Buddha.

units.zh: 清泰，廢帝年號也。
units.en: Qingtai was Emperor Fei's reign title.
units.literal: Qingtai was Emperor Fei's reign title.

units.zh: 人有戲胤孫曰：「公素慕韓愈為人，而常誦傅奕之論，今反佞佛，是佛佞公邪，公佞佛邪？」
units.en: Someone joked with Yinxun, saying: "Your Lordship has always admired Han Yu as a man and often recited Fu Yi's arguments. Now instead you fawn on the Buddha. Is the Buddha fawning on you, or are you fawning on the Buddha?"
units.literal: Someone jested with Yinxun, saying, "You have always admired Han Yu as a man and often recited Fu Yi's treatises; now you turn to fawning on the Buddha—is it the Buddha fawning on you, or you fawning on the Buddha?

units.zh: 胤孫答曰：「豈知非佛佞我也？」
units.en: Yinxun replied, "Who is to say the Buddha is not fawning on me?"
units.literal: Yinxun answered, "How do you know it is not the Buddha fawning on me?"

units.zh: 時人傳以為笑。
units.en: The story made the rounds as a joke.
units.literal: People of the time spread it about as a laughing matter.

units.zh: 後以太子賓客分司居於洛陽，周廣順中卒。
units.en: He later lived in Luoyang as guest of the heir apparent with a separate commission and died in the Guangshun era of Zhou.
units.literal: Later he lived in Luoyang as Guest of the Heir Apparent with a separate commission; he died in the Guangshun era of Zhou.

units.zh: 胤孫卒後，其家婢有為胤孫語者。
units.en: After Yinxun's death, a maid in his household began to speak in his voice.
units.literal: After Yinxun died, a maid in his household spoke in Yinxun's voice.

units.zh: 初，崔協為明宗相，在位無所發明，既死，而有降語其家，胤孫又然。
units.en: Earlier, when Cui Xie had served Mingzong as chancellor, he had accomplished nothing in office. After his death his household received spirit messages, and the same happened with Yinxun.
units.literal: Earlier, when Cui Xie was Mingzong's chancellor, in office he accomplished nothing noteworthy; after his death there was spirit-descended speech in his household, and Yinxun's case was the same.

units.zh: 時人嘲之曰：「生不能言，死而後語」云。
units.en: People mocked them with the saying: "Alive they could not speak; dead they speak at last."
units.literal: People of the time mocked them, saying, "Alive they could not speak; dead they speak afterward," and so on.

units.zh: 姚顗，字百真，京兆長安人也。
units.en: Yao Yi, courtesy name Baizhen, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Yao Yi, courtesy name Baizhen, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 少蠢，不修容止，時人莫之知，中條山處士司空圖一見以為奇，以其女妻之。
units.en: As a youth he seemed dull and paid no attention to his bearing, and no one took notice of him. Sikong Tu, a recluse of Mount Zhongtiao, saw him once, thought him remarkable, and gave him his daughter in marriage.
units.literal: In youth he was dull and did not cultivate deportment; people of the time did not know him. The recluse of Zhongtiao Mountain, Sikong Tu, upon one meeting thought him extraordinary and gave him his daughter in marriage.

units.zh: 舉進士，事梁為翰林學士、中書舍人。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination and served Later Liang as Hanlin academician and secretariat drafter.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served Liang as Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 唐莊宗滅梁，貶復州司馬，已而以為左散騎常侍兼吏部侍郎、尚書左丞。
units.en: When Zhuangzong of Tang destroyed Later Liang, Yi was demoted to military adjutant of Fuzhou, but was soon restored as left regular attendant with concurrent posts as vice minister of personnel and left assistant director in the Ministry of State Affairs.
units.literal: When Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, [Yi] was demoted to military adjutant of Fuzhou; before long he was made Left Regular Attendant with concurrent appointment as Vice Minister of Personnel and Left Assistant Director in the Ministry of State Affairs.

units.zh: 廢帝欲擇宰相，選當時清望官知名於世者，得盧文紀及顗，乃拜顗中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: When Emperor Fei wished to choose a chancellor, he looked among the most eminent officials of the day and settled on Lu Wenji and Yi. Yi was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor.
units.literal: Emperor Fei wished to choose a chancellor, selecting from officials of clear reputation famous in the world at the time; he obtained Lu Wenji and Yi, and appointed Yi Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 顗為人仁恕，不知錢陌銖兩之數，禦家無法，在相位齪齪無所為。
units.en: Yi was kindly and forgiving but knew nothing of money down to the last cash or ounce. He kept no order in his household. As chancellor he fussed over trifles and achieved nothing.
units.literal: Yi as a man was benevolent and forgiving; he did not know the numbers of cash strings and ounce-weights; in managing his household he had no method; in the chancellorship he was cramped and accomplished nothing.

units.zh: 唐制吏部分為三銓，尚書一人曰尚書銓，侍郎二人曰中銓、東銓。
units.en: Under Tang regulations the Ministry of Personnel was divided into three selection boards: the minister's board, the central board, and the eastern board.
units.literal: Under Tang regulations the Ministry of Personnel was divided into three selection boards: one minister called the Minister's Board, and two vice ministers called the Central Board and the Eastern Board.

units.zh: 每歲集以孟冬三旬，而選盡季春之月。
units.en: Each year the registry opened in the three ten-day periods of early winter, and selections were finished by late spring.
units.literal: Each year candidates were assembled in the three ten-day periods of early winter, and selections were completed by the last month of spring.

units.zh: 天成中，馮道為相，建言：「天下未一，選人歲才數百，而吏部三銓分註，雖曰故事，其實徒繁而無益。」
units.en: During the Tiancheng era, when Feng Dao was chancellor, he proposed: "The realm is not yet unified, and those selected each year number only a few hundred. The Ministry of Personnel's three selection boards make separate annotations; although this is called precedent, in fact it is only cumbersome and has no benefit."
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era, Feng Dao as chancellor submitted a proposal: "The realm is not yet unified; candidates each year number only in the hundreds, yet the Ministry of Personnel's three boards assign posts separately—although called established practice, in truth it is merely cumbersome and without benefit.

units.zh: 始詔三銓合為一，而尚書、侍郎共行選事。
units.en: An edict merged the three boards into one, with the minister and vice ministers conducting selections together.
units.literal: An edict was first issued to merge the three boards into one, with the minister and vice ministers jointly conducting selection affairs.

units.zh: 至顗與盧文紀為相，復奏分銓為三。
units.en: When Yi and Lu Wenji became chancellors, they memorialized to divide the boards into three once again.
units.literal: When Yi and Lu Wenji became chancellors, they again memorialized to divide the boards into three.

units.zh: 而循資、長定舊格，歲久多舛，因增損之。
units.en: The old rules for seniority and fixed promotion standards had grown corrupt with age, so they revised them.
units.literal: The old standards for following seniority and fixed long-term rules, after many years, had many errors; they therefore added to and reduced them.

units.zh: 選人多不便之，往往邀遮宰相，喧訴不遜，顗等無如之何，廢帝為下詔書禁止。
units.en: Candidates were displeased and often waylaid the chancellors with loud, insolent protests. Yi and his colleagues could do nothing, until Emperor Fei issued an edict forbidding such behavior.
units.literal: Candidates were mostly displeased with this; they often intercepted and blocked the chancellors, clamoring and complaining without deference. Yi and the others could do nothing about it, and Emperor Fei issued an edict forbidding it.

units.zh: 晉高祖立，罷顗為戶部尚書。
units.en: When Gaozu of Later Jin took the throne, Yi was removed to minister of revenue.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, Yi was removed and made Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 卒，年七十五，卒之日，家無餘貲，屍不能斂，官為赗贈乃能斂，聞者哀憐之。
units.en: He died at seventy-five. On the day of his death his household had nothing left; his body could not be buried until the government provided funeral gifts. All who heard of it pitied him.
units.literal: He died, aged seventy-five. On the day of his death the household had no surplus funds; the corpse could not be encoffined until the government provided funeral gifts, and those who heard of it pitied him.

units.zh: 劉嶽，字昭輔，洛陽人也。
units.en: Liu Yue, courtesy name Zhaofu, was a native of Luoyang.
units.literal: Liu Yue, courtesy name Zhaofu, was a native of Luoyang.

units.zh: 唐民部尚書政會之八代孫，崇龜、崇望其諸父也。
units.en: He was the eighth-generation descendant of Zhenghui, Tang minister of the people's affairs; Chonggui and Chongwang were his uncles.
units.literal: He was the eighth-generation descendant of Tang's Minister of the People's Affairs Zhenghui; Chonggui and Chongwang were his paternal uncles.

units.zh: 嶽名家子，好學，敏於文辭，善談論。
units.en: Yue came from a distinguished family, loved learning, wrote with quick facility, and was a gifted conversationalist.
units.literal: Yue was the son of an eminent family, loved learning, was quick in literary composition, and was skilled at discussion.

units.zh: 舉進士，事梁為左拾遺、侍御史。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination and served Later Liang as left reminder and attending censor.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served Liang as Left Reminder and Attending Censor.

units.zh: 末帝時，為翰林學士，累官至兵部侍郎。
units.en: Under the last Liang emperor he became Hanlin academician and rose to vice minister of war.
units.literal: In the time of the Last Emperor he was Hanlin Academician and rose in succession to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 梁亡，貶均州司馬，復用為太子詹事。
units.en: When Later Liang fell he was demoted to military adjutant of Junzhou, then restored as grand steward of the heir apparent.
units.literal: When Liang perished he was demoted to military adjutant of Junzhou; he was again employed as Grand Steward of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 唐明宗時，為吏部侍郎。
units.en: Under Tang Emperor Mingzong he served as vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: In the time of Tang Emperor Mingzong he was Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 故事，吏部文武官告身，皆輸朱膠紙軸錢然後給，其品高者則賜之，貧者不能輸錢，往往但得敕牒而無告身。
units.en: By custom, civil and military appointment credentials required payment for paste, paper, and scroll rods before issue. High-ranking officials received them as gifts, but the poor often could pay only for the edict copy and never received the formal credential.
units.literal: By established practice, civil and military appointment credentials from the Ministry of Personnel all required payment of fees for vermilion paste, paper, and scroll rods before being issued; those of high rank were granted them, but the poor could not pay and often received only the edict copy without the formal credential.

units.zh: 五代之亂，因以為常，官卑者無復給告身，中書但錄其制辭，編為敕甲。
units.en: The chaos of the Five Dynasties made this the norm. Low officials no longer received credentials at all; the Secretariat merely recorded appointment texts in edict registers.
units.literal: In the chaos of the Five Dynasties this became the norm; low-ranking officials no longer received credentials, and the Secretariat merely recorded the appointment texts and compiled them as edict registers.

units.zh: 嶽建言，以謂「制辭或任其材能，或褒其功行，或申以訓誡，而受官者既不給告身，皆不知受命之所以然，非王言所以告詔也。
units.en: Yue proposed, saying, "Appointment texts sometimes assign office according to a man's talents and abilities, sometimes praise his achievements and conduct, and sometimes extend instruction and admonition. Yet since those who receive office are not issued appointment credentials, none know why they have received the command. This is not the way royal words should announce commands.
units.literal: Yue submitted a proposal, saying, "Appointment texts sometimes assign duties according to talent, sometimes praise conduct and achievement, sometimes deliver admonition and instruction—yet those receiving office are not given credentials and none know why they have received their commission. This is not how royal words ought to announce and instruct.

units.zh: 請一切賜之。」
units.en: I request that they all be granted."
units.literal: He requested that all be granted them.

units.zh: 由是百官皆賜告身，自嶽始也。
units.en: From then on all officials received credentials—a reform that began with Yue.
units.literal: Thereupon all hundred officials were granted credentials—this began with Yue.

units.zh: 宰相馮道世本田家，狀貌質野，朝士多笑其陋。
units.en: Chancellor Feng Dao came from a farming family and looked plain and rustic; many courtiers mocked his uncouth appearance.
units.literal: The chancellor Feng Dao came from a farming family by birth; his appearance was plain and rustic, and many court gentlemen laughed at his uncouthness.

units.zh: 道旦入朝，兵部侍郎任贊與嶽在其後，道行數反顧，贊問嶽：「道反顧何為？」
units.en: One morning Dao entered court, with Vice Minister of War Ren Zan and Yue behind him. Dao repeatedly looked back as he walked. Zan asked Yue: "Why is Dao looking back?"
units.literal: One morning Dao entered court; the Vice Minister of War Ren Zan and Yue were behind him. Dao walked several paces and repeatedly looked back. Zan asked Yue, "Why does Dao keep looking back?

units.zh: 嶽曰：「遺下《兔園冊》爾。」
units.en: Yue said, "He left his Rabbit Garden Manual behind."
units.literal: Yue said, "He left behind the Rabbit Garden Manual, that's all."

units.zh: 《兔園冊》者，鄉校俚儒教田夫牧子之所誦也，故嶽舉以誚道。
units.en: The Rabbit Garden Manual was the primer village schoolmasters used for farmers' sons—Yue cited it to ridicule Dao.
units.literal: The Rabbit Garden Manual was what village-school rustic scholars had farmers' sons and herdsboys recite; Yue therefore cited it to mock Dao.

units.zh: 道聞之大怒，徙嶽秘書監。
units.en: Dao heard of it and, furious, transferred Yue to director of the Palace Library.
units.literal: When Dao heard of it he was greatly enraged and transferred Yue to Director of the Palace Library.

units.zh: 其後李愚為相，遷嶽太常卿。
units.en: Later, when Li Yu became chancellor, Yue was promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: Later, when Li Yu became chancellor, Yue was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 初，鄭餘慶嘗采唐士庶吉兇書疏之式，雜以當時家人之禮，為《書儀》兩卷。
units.en: Earlier, Zheng Yuqing had compiled Tang models for letters of congratulation and condolence, mixed with contemporary household ritual, into two fascicles called Ceremonial Forms.
units.literal: At the beginning, Zheng Yuqing once collected Tang forms for auspicious and inauspicious letters and memorials of gentlemen and commoners, mixed with contemporary household ritual, and made two fascicles of Ceremonial Forms.

units.zh: 明宗見其起復、冥昏之制，嘆曰：「儒者所以隆孝悌而敦風俗，且無金革之事，起復可乎？
units.en: Mingzong read its rules on resuming office during mourning and on weddings during mourning and sighed: "Confucians exist to exalt filial piety and good custom. With no war under way, how can resuming office during mourning be right?
units.literal: Mingzong saw its regulations on resuming office during mourning and on wedding rites during mourning, and sighed, saying, "Confucians exist to exalt filial piety and brotherly duty and to encourage custom—moreover there are no military campaigns; can resuming office during mourning be permissible?

units.zh: 婚，吉禮也，用於死者可乎？」
units.en: Marriage is an auspicious rite. How can it be used for the dead?"
units.literal: Marriage is an auspicious rite—can it be used for the dead?

units.zh: 乃詔嶽選文學通知古今之士，共刪定之。
units.en: He ordered Yue to select learned men versed in past and present to revise the work jointly.
units.literal: He thereupon ordered Yue to select literary men versed in past and present to revise and fix it together.

units.zh: 嶽與太常博士段颙、田敏等增損其書，而其事出鄙俚，皆當時家人女子傳習所見，往往轉失其本，然猶時有《禮》之遺制。
units.en: Yue worked with court academicians Duan Yong, Tian Min, and others to revise the book. Much of it came from vulgar household custom, passed on by women of the time and often far from the original, though traces of the canonical Rites still survived.
units.literal: Yue, together with the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians Duan Yong, Tian Min, and others, added to and reduced the book; yet its matters came from vulgar custom—all that household women of the time transmitted and practiced—and often further lost the original, yet still at times preserved remnants of the Rites.

units.zh: 其後亡失，愈不可究其本末，其婚禮親迎，有女坐婿鞍合髻之說，尤為不經。
units.en: Later portions were lost, and the work grew ever harder to trace. Its wedding rite included the bride sitting on the groom's saddle and joining their hair-knots—especially absurd.
units.literal: Later it was lost, and ever less could its beginning and end be traced; in its wedding rite for the groom's receiving the bride, there was the account of the bride sitting on the groom's saddle and joining hair-knots—especially uncanonical.

units.zh: 公卿之家，頗遵用之。
units.en: Great families largely followed it nonetheless.
units.literal: Families of dukes and ministers largely followed and used it.

units.zh: 至其久也，又益訛謬可笑，其類甚多。
units.en: Over time it grew ever more corrupt and ridiculous in countless ways.
units.literal: As time went on, it further grew erroneous and laughable; such cases were many.

units.zh: 嶽卒於官，年五十六，贈吏部尚書。
units.en: Yue died in office at fifty-six and was posthumously made minister of personnel.
units.literal: Yue died in office, aged fifty-six, and was posthumously given the title of Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 子溫叟。
units.en: His son was Wensou.
units.literal: His son was Wensou.

units.zh: 嗚呼，甚矣，人之好為禮也！
units.en: Alas, how passionately people cling to ritual performance!
units.literal: Alas, how extreme is people's fondness for performing ritual!

units.zh: 在上者不以禮示之，使人不見其本，而傳其習俗之失者，尚拳拳而行之。
units.en: Those in authority fail to teach ritual properly, so people never see its roots, yet they still earnestly follow corrupted custom.
units.literal: Those above do not display ritual to show the way, so that people do not see its root, yet they still earnestly practice what transmits the errors of custom.

units.zh: 五代干戈之亂，不暇於禮久矣！
units.en: The Five Dynasties had long been too torn by war to attend to ritual!
units.literal: In the Five Dynasties' chaos of arms and warfare, there had long been no leisure for ritual!

units.zh: 明宗武君，出於夷狄，而不通文字，乃能有意使民知禮。
units.en: Mingzong was a martial ruler of barbarian origin who could not read, yet he still wished to teach the people ritual.
units.literal: Mingzong was a martial ruler who came from barbarian lands and did not understand writing, yet he could intend to make the people know ritual.

units.zh: 而嶽等皆當時儒者，卒無所發明，但因其書增損而已。
units.en: Yet Yue and his colleagues, though leading Confucians of the day, clarified nothing in the end and merely revised that book.
units.literal: Yet Yue and the others were all Confucians of the time and in the end accomplished no new clarification—they only added to and reduced that book.

units.zh: 然其後世士庶吉兇，皆取嶽書以為法，而十又轉失其三四也，可勝嘆哉！
units.en: Later generations of gentlemen and commoners alike took Yue's book as their standard for congratulation and condolence, yet three or four parts in ten were lost again in transmission. How lamentable!
units.literal: Yet later generations of gentlemen and commoners in auspicious and inauspicious matters all took Yue's book as their standard, and of ten parts three or four were further lost in transmission—how much is there to lament!

units.zh: 馬縞，不知其世家，少舉明經，又舉宏詞。
units.en: Ma Gao's lineage is unknown. In youth he passed the Mingjing examination and also the Hongci examination.
units.literal: Ma Gao—his distinguished family is unknown. In youth he passed the Mingjing examination and also passed the Hongci examination.

units.zh: 事梁為太常少卿，以知禮見稱於世。
units.en: He served Later Liang as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was renowned for his knowledge of ritual.
units.literal: He served Liang as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was praised in the world for his knowledge of ritual.

units.zh: 唐莊宗時，累遷中書舍人、刑部侍郎、權判太常卿。
units.en: Under Zhuangzong of Tang he rose to secretariat drafter, vice minister of justice, and acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: In the time of Tang Emperor Zhuangzong he was promoted in succession to Secretariat Drafter, Vice Minister of Justice, and Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 明宗入立，繼唐太祖、莊宗而不立親廟。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne after Tang Taizu and Zhuangzong, he did not establish a temple to his own ancestors.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, succeeding Tang's Taizu and Zhuangzong, he did not establish a temple to his own forebears.

units.zh: 縞言：「漢諸侯王入繼統者，必別立親廟，光武皇帝立四廟於南陽，請如漢故事，立廟以申孝享。」
units.en: Gao said: "When Han feudal princes entered to succeed to the imperial line, they always separately established temples to their own parents. Emperor Guangwu established four temples at Nanyang. I request that Han precedent be followed and temples established to extend filial sacrifice."
units.literal: Gao said, "Han feudal kings who entered to succeed the imperial line always separately established temples to their own forebears; Emperor Guangwu established four temples at Nanyang. I request following Han precedent to establish temples and thereby extend filial offerings.

units.zh: 明宗下其議，禮部尚書蕭頃等請如縞議。
units.en: Mingzong referred the proposal for discussion. Minister of Rites Xiao Qing and others supported Gao's plan.
units.literal: Mingzong sent down his proposal for discussion; the Minister of Rites Xiao Qing and others requested following Gao's proposal.

units.zh: 宰相鄭玨等議引漢桓、靈為比，以謂靈帝尊其祖解瀆亭侯淑為孝元皇，父萇為孝仁皇，請下有司定謚四代祖考為皇，置園陵如漢故事。
units.en: Chancellor Zheng Jue and others cited Emperors Huan and Ling of Han, noting that Ling had honored his grandfather as Emperor Xiaoyuan and his father as Emperor Xiaoren. They asked the proper offices to posthumously title four generations of ancestors as emperor and establish gardens and tombs as in Han practice.
units.literal: The chancellor Zheng Jue and others debated, citing Han's Emperors Huan and Ling as parallels, holding that Emperor Ling honored his grandfather, Marquis Shu of Jiedu Pavilion, as Emperor Xiaoyuan, and his father Chang as Emperor Xiaoren; they requested sending down to the relevant offices to fix posthumous titles for four generations of ancestors as Huang, and establishing gardens and tombs as in Han precedent.

units.zh: 事下太常，博士王丕議漢桓帝尊祖為孝穆皇帝，父為孝崇皇帝。
units.en: The matter went to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Academician Wang Pi noted that Emperor Huan of Han had honored his grandfather as Emperor Xiaomu and his father as Emperor Xiaochong.
units.literal: The matter was sent down to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the academician Wang Pi debated that Emperor Huan of Han honored his grandfather as Emperor Xiaomu and his father as Emperor Xiaochong.

units.zh: 縞以謂孝穆、孝崇有皇而無帝，惟吳孫皓尊其父和為文皇帝，不可以為法。
units.en: Gao argued that Xiaomu and Xiaochong bore the title emperor in name but not in full form, and that only Sun Hao of Wu had honored his father as Emperor Wen—a precedent that could not be followed.
units.literal: Gao held that Xiaomu and Xiaochong had Huang but not Di; only Wu's Sun Hao honored his father He as Emperor Wen—this cannot serve as a model.

units.zh: 右僕射李琪等議與縞同。
units.en: Right vice director Li Qi and others agreed with Gao.
units.literal: The Right Vice Director Li Qi and others debated in agreement with Gao.

units.zh: 明宗詔曰：「五帝不相襲禮，三王不相沿樂，惟皇與帝，異世殊稱。
units.en: Mingzong's edict read: "The Five Emperors did not inherit one another's ritual; the Three Kings did not continue one another's music. Huang and Di are titles of different ages with distinct names.
units.literal: Mingzong's edict said, "The Five Emperors did not inherit one another's ritual; the Three Kings did not continue one another's music—only Huang and Di are titles of different ages and distinct appellations.

units.zh: 爰自嬴秦，已兼厥號，朕居九五之位，為億兆之尊，奈何總二名於眇躬，惜一字於先世。」
units.en: Since the Qin dynasty the titles have been combined. I occupy the throne of nine and five and serve as lord of the myriad people. How can I combine the two names in my small person, yet begrudge one word to former generations?"
units.literal: From Qin of Ying onward the titles were already combined; I occupy the position of the Nine-Five, the honor of the hundred millions—how can I gather both names upon my slight person and be sparing of a single character for former generations?

units.zh: 乃命宰臣集百官於中書，各陳所見。
units.en: He ordered the chief ministers to assemble all officials at the Secretariat so each could state his view.
units.literal: He thereupon ordered the chief ministers to assemble the hundred officials at the Secretariat, each to state his view.

units.zh: 李琪等請尊祖禰為皇帝，曾高為皇。
units.en: Li Qi and others proposed honoring grandfather and father as emperors and more remote ancestors as emperor in abbreviated form.
units.literal: Li Qi and others requested honoring grandfather and father as Huangdi and great-great-grandfather and great-grandfather as Huang.

units.zh: 宰相鄭玨合群議奏曰：「禮非天降而本人情，可止可行，有損有益。
units.en: Chancellor Zheng Jue summarized the group's views: "Ritual does not descend from Heaven but arises from human feeling. It may be practiced or set aside, to harm or to benefit.
units.literal: The chancellor Zheng Jue combined the group's discussion and memorialized, saying, "Ritual does not descend from Heaven but arises from human feeling; it may be stopped or practiced, with harm or benefit.

units.zh: 今議者引古，以漢為據，漢之所制，夫復何依？
units.en: The debaters cite antiquity and take Han as their authority—but upon what further authority does Han itself rest?
units.literal: Now the debaters cite antiquity and take Han as their basis—what further basis is there in what Han established?

units.zh: 開元時，尊臯陶為德明皇帝，涼武昭王為興聖皇帝，皆立廟京師，此唐家故事也。
units.en: In the Kaiyuan era, Gao Yao was honored as Emperor Deming and the Martial Illustrious King of Liang as Emperor Xingsheng, with temples established in the capital. That was Tang precedent.
units.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Gao Yao was honored as Emperor Deming and the Martial Illustrious King of Liang as Emperor Xingsheng; temples were all established in the capital—this is Tang family precedent.

units.zh: 臣請四代祖考皆加帝如詔旨，而立廟京師。」
units.en: Your servant requests that the ancestors of four generations all be given the title Di according to the edict's intent, and that temples be established in the capital."
units.literal: Your subject requests that four generations of ancestors all receive Di as in the edict's intent, and that temples be established in the capital.

units.zh: 詔可其加帝，而立廟應州。
units.en: An edict approved the full imperial titles and established temples at Yingzhou.
units.literal: An edict approved adding Di, and established temples at Yingzhou.

units.zh: 劉嶽修《書儀》，其所增損，皆決於縞。
units.en: When Liu Yue revised the Ceremonial Forms, Gao decided every addition and deletion.
units.literal: When Liu Yue revised the Ceremonial Forms, all additions and reductions were decided by Gao.

units.zh: 縞又言：「缞麻喪紀，所以別親疏，辨嫌疑。
units.en: Gao also said: "Hemp mourning and mourning regulations are what distinguish closeness and distance of kin and resolve doubts and suspicions.
units.literal: Gao also said, "Hemp mourning grades exist to distinguish near from distant kin and to clarify what is doubtful.

units.zh: 《禮》，叔嫂無服，推而遠之也。
units.en: The Rites prescribe no mourning between brother's wife and husband's younger brother, pushing such relations away by design.
units.literal: The Rites state that brother's wife and husband's younger brother have no mourning obligation—pushing them away in distance.

units.zh: 唐太宗時，有司議為兄之妻服小功五月，今有司給假為大功九月，非是。」
units.en: In the time of Tang Taizong, the proper offices debated wearing xiaogong mourning for five months for an elder brother's wife. Now the proper offices grant leave as dagong for nine months. This is incorrect."
units.literal: In the time of Tang Emperor Taizong the relevant offices debated wearing xiaogong for five months for an elder brother's wife; now the relevant offices grant leave for dagong of nine months—this is not correct.

units.zh: 廢帝下其議，太常博士段颙議「嫂服給假以大功者，令文也，令與禮異者非一，而喪服之不同者五。
units.en: Emperor Fei referred the proposal for discussion. Academician Duan Yong of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices argued, "That leave for mourning an elder brother's wife is granted as dagong is the text of the statute. There is more than one place where statute and ritual differ, and there are five cases where mourning garments differ.
units.literal: Emperor Fei sent down his proposal for discussion. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Duan Yong debated: "Granting leave for sister-in-law mourning as dagong is statutory text; statutes and rites differ in more than one place, and mourning garments differ in five cases.

units.zh: 《禮》，姨舅皆服小功，令皆大功。
units.en: The Rites prescribe xiaogong for maternal aunt and uncle; the statutes prescribe dagong.
units.literal: The Rites prescribe xiaogong for maternal aunt and maternal uncle; the statutes all prescribe dagong.

units.zh: 妻父母婿外甥皆服緦，令皆小功。
units.en: The Rites prescribe si for wife's parents, son-in-law, and sister's son; the statutes prescribe xiaogong.
units.literal: Wife's parents, son-in-law, and sister's son all wear si in the Rites; the statutes all prescribe xiaogong.

units.zh: 禮、令之不可同如此。」
units.en: That ritual and statute cannot be made the same is like this."
units.literal: Thus ritual and statute cannot be made the same."

units.zh: 右贊善大夫趙咸又議曰：「喪，與其易也，寧戚。
units.en: Right mentor of goodness Zhao Xian argued further, quoting the classic: "In mourning, better than ease is grief.
units.literal: The Right Mentor of Goodness Zhao Xian again debated, saying, "In mourning, better than ease is grief.

units.zh: 《儀禮》五服，或以名加，或因尊制，推恩引義，各有所當。
units.en: The Ceremonial Rites' five mourning grades sometimes follow name, sometimes follow rank; extending grace and drawing on principle, each has its proper measure.
units.literal: The Ceremonial Rites' five grades of mourning sometimes add by name, sometimes regulate by honor; extending grace and drawing on principle, each has its proper application.

units.zh: 據《禮》為兄之子妻服大功，今為兄之子母服小功，是輕重失其倫也。
units.en: The Rites prescribe dagong for an elder brother's son's wife but xiaogong for his mother—a reversal of proper gradation.
units.literal: According to the Rites, one wears dagong for an elder brother's son's wife; now one wears xiaogong for an elder brother's son's mother—this is a failure of heavy and light in proper order.

units.zh: 以名則兄子之妻疏，因尊則嫂非卑，嫂服大功，其來已久。
units.en: By name an elder brother's son's wife is more distant kin; by rank a sister-in-law is not lowly. Dagong mourning for a sister-in-law is long established.
units.literal: By name the elder brother's son's wife is more distant; by honor the sister-in-law is not lowly—dagong for a sister-in-law has long been established.

units.zh: 令，國之典，不可滅也。」
units.en: Statute is the law of the state and cannot be abolished."
units.literal: The statute is the state's canon and cannot be abolished."

units.zh: 司封郎中曹琛，請下其議，並以《禮》、令之違者定議。
units.en: Bureau director of enfeoffment Cao Chen asked that the discussion be referred downward and a decision fixed for every conflict between ritual and statute.
units.literal: The Bureau Director of Enfeoffment Cao Chen requested sending down the discussion and fixing a decision on all cases where the Rites and statutes conflict.

units.zh: 詔尚書省集百官議。
units.en: An edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to assemble all officials for discussion.
units.literal: An edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to assemble the hundred officials for discussion.

units.zh: 左僕射劉句等議曰：「令於喪服無正文，而嫂服給大功假，乃假寧附令，而敕無年月，請凡喪服皆以《開元禮》為定，下太常具五服制度，附於令。」
units.en: Left vice director Liu Xu and others argued: "The statute has no main text on mourning garments, and dagong leave for a sister-in-law is only leave attached to the statute, while the edict has no year or month. We request that all mourning garments be fixed according to the Kaiyuan Rites, and that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices be ordered to prepare the five mourning-grade system and attach it to the statute."
units.literal: The Left Vice Director Liu Xu and others debated, saying, "The statute has no main text on mourning garments, while leave for sister-in-law mourning as dagong is leave for rest attached to the statute, and the edict has no months and years. We request that all mourning garments be fixed according to the Kaiyuan Rites, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices be ordered to prepare the five-grade mourning system and attach it to the statute.

units.zh: 令有五服，自縞始也。
units.en: The statute's five mourning grades began with Gao.
units.literal: The statute's five grades of mourning began with Gao.

units.zh: 縞明宗時嘗坐覆獄不當，貶綏州司馬。
units.en: Under Mingzong, Gao once mishandled a case review and was demoted to military adjutant of Suizhou.
units.literal: In Mingzong's time Gao once sat in judgment on a case review improperly and was demoted to military adjutant of Suizhou.

units.zh: 復為太子賓客，遷戶部、兵部侍郎。
units.en: He was restored as guest of the heir apparent and promoted to vice minister of revenue and vice minister of war.
units.literal: He was again made Guest of the Heir Apparent and was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 盧文紀作相，以其迂儒鄙之，改國子祭酒。
units.en: When Lu Wenji became chancellor, he despised Gao as a pedantic scholar and reassigned him to rector of the Imperial University.
units.literal: When Lu Wenji became chancellor, he despised him as a pedantic Confucian and changed his post to Rector of the Imperial University.

units.zh: 卒，年八十，贈兵部尚書。
units.en: He died at eighty and was posthumously made minister of war.
units.literal: He died, aged eighty, and was posthumously given the title of Minister of War.

units.zh: ○崔居儉
units.en: Cui Jujian
units.literal: Cui Jujian

units.zh: 崔居儉，清河人也。
units.en: Cui Jujian was from Qinghe.
units.literal: Cui Jujian was a man of Qinghe.

units.zh: 祖蠡、父蕘皆為唐名臣。
units.en: His grandfather Li and father Rao were both renowned Tang ministers.
units.literal: His grandfather Li and father Rao were both famous Tang ministers.

units.zh: 居儉美文辭，風骨清秀，少舉進士。
units.en: Jujian wrote elegant prose with a refined bearing and passed the jinshi examination in his youth.
units.literal: Jujian was skilled in literary composition, with clear and refined bearing; in youth he passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 梁貞明中，為中書舍人、翰林學士、御史中丞。
units.en: During the Zhenming era of Later Liang he served as secretariat drafter, Hanlin academician, and censor-in-chief.
units.literal: In the Zhenming era of Liang he was Secretariat Drafter, Hanlin Academician, and Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 唐莊宗時，為刑部侍郎、太常卿。
units.en: Under Zhuangzong of Tang he was vice minister of justice and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: In the time of Tang Emperor Zhuangzong he was Vice Minister of Justice and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 崔氏自後魏、隋、唐與盧、鄭皆為甲族，吉兇之事，各著家禮。
units.en: The Cui clan, like the Lu and Zheng clans, had been a leading family since Northern Wei, Sui, and Tang, with household rituals recorded for every auspicious and inauspicious occasion.
units.literal: The Cui clan from Later Wei, Sui, and Tang, together with the Lu and Zheng clans, were all leading families; in auspicious and inauspicious matters each had its own household ritual recorded.

units.zh: 至其後世子孫，專以門望自高，為世所嫉。
units.en: Later descendants relied solely on family prestige and were widely resented.
units.literal: By the time of their later descendants, they relied solely on family prestige to hold themselves high and were envied by the world.

units.zh: 明宗崩，居儉以故事為禮儀使，居儉以祖諱蠡，辭不受，宰相馮道即徙居儉為秘書監。
units.en: When Mingzong died, Jujian should by precedent have become commissioner of rites, but he declined because his grandfather's taboo name was Li. Chancellor Feng Dao immediately reassigned him to director of the Palace Library.
units.literal: When Mingzong died, Jujian by precedent ought to have become Commissioner of Rites; Jujian declined on the ground of his grandfather's taboo name Li, and the chancellor Feng Dao immediately transferred Jujian to Director of the Palace Library.

units.zh: 居儉歷兵、吏部侍郎、尚書左丞、戶部尚書。
units.en: Jujian served as vice minister of war, vice minister of personnel, left assistant director in the Ministry of State Affairs, and minister of revenue.
units.literal: Jujian served in succession as Vice Minister of War, Vice Minister of Personnel, Left Assistant Director in the Ministry of State Affairs, and Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 晉天福四年卒，年七十，贈右僕射。
units.en: He died in the fourth year of Tianfu of Later Jin at seventy and was posthumously made right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.
units.literal: He died in the fourth year of Tianfu of Jin, aged seventy, and was posthumously given the title of Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 居儉拙於為生，居顯官，衣常乏，死之日貧不能葬，聞者哀之。
units.en: Jujian was inept at providing for himself. Though he held high office, he often lacked proper clothing. At his death he was too poor to be buried, and all who heard pitied him.
units.literal: Jujian was clumsy at making a living; though he held eminent office, his clothing was often lacking; on the day of his death he was too poor to be buried, and those who heard of it pitied him.

units.zh: 崔棁，字子文，深州安平人也。
units.en: Cui Zhuo, courtesy name Ziwen, was a native of Anping in Shenzhou.
units.literal: Cui Zhuo, courtesy name Ziwen, was a native of Anping in Shenzhou.

units.zh: 父涿，唐末為刑部郎中。
units.en: His father Zhuo was a bureau director in the Ministry of Justice at the end of Tang.
units.literal: His father Zhuo was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice at the end of Tang.

units.zh: 棁少好學，頗涉經史，工於文辭。
units.en: Zhuo loved learning from youth, read widely in the classics and histories, and wrote with skill.
units.literal: Zhuo in youth loved learning, was broadly versed in the classics and histories, and was skilled in literary composition.

units.zh: 遭世亂，寓居於滑臺，不遊裏巷者十餘年，人罕識其面。
units.en: During the turmoil of the age he lodged at Huatai and did not venture into the streets for more than ten years, so few people knew his face.
units.literal: Encountering the chaos of the age, he lodged at Huatai and did not wander the lanes and alleys for more than ten years; people rarely knew his face.

units.zh: 梁貞明三年，舉進士甲科，開封尹王瓚辟掌奏記。
units.en: In the third year of Zhenming of Later Liang he passed the jinshi examination in the first class, and Wang Zan, metropolitan governor of Kaifeng, recruited him as master of memorials.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhenming of Liang he passed the jinshi examination in the first class; Wang Zan, metropolitan governor of Kaifeng, recruited him as master of memorials.

units.zh: 棁性至孝，其父涿病，不肯服藥，曰：「死生有命，何用藥為？」
units.en: Zhuo was profoundly filial. When his father Zhuo fell ill, he refused medicine and said: "Life and death are fated. What use is medicine?"
units.literal: Zhuo was by nature extremely filial. His father Zhuo fell ill and refused to take medicine, saying, "Life and death have their mandate—what use is medicine?

units.zh: 棁屢進醫藥，不納。
units.en: Zhuo repeatedly brought physicians and medicine, but his father would not accept them.
units.literal: Zhuo repeatedly presented physicians and medicine; [his father] would not accept them.

units.zh: 每賓客問疾者，棁輒迎拜門外，泣涕而告之，涿終不服藥而卒。
units.en: Whenever guests came to inquire after his father's health, Zhuo would meet them at the gate with bows and tears. The father never took medicine and died.
units.literal: Whenever guests came to inquire after his illness, Zhuo would go out to the gate to receive and bow to them, weeping and telling them; Zhuo the father ultimately would not take medicine and died.

units.zh: 棁居喪哀毀，服除，唐明宗以為監察御史，不拜，逾年再命，乃拜。
units.en: Zhuo mourned so deeply that he was nearly wasted away. When mourning ended, Mingzong appointed him attending censor, but he declined. More than a year later a second appointment came, and he accepted.
units.literal: Zhuo in mourning was grief-stricken to the point of emaciation. When mourning ended, Tang Emperor Mingzong appointed him Attending Censor; he did not accept. After more than a year he was appointed again, and then he accepted.

units.zh: 累遷都官郎中、翰林學士。
units.en: He rose to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice and Hanlin academician.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice and Hanlin Academician.

units.zh: 晉高祖時，以戶部侍郎為學士承旨，權知天福二年貢舉。
units.en: Under Gaozu of Later Jin he served as vice minister of revenue and chief academician, with provisional charge of the second-year Tianfu civil service examination.
units.literal: In the time of Gaozu of Jin, as Vice Minister of Revenue he became Chief Academician and was given provisional charge of the Tianfu second-year examination.

units.zh: 初，棁為學士，嘗草制，為宰相桑維翰所改。
units.en: Early in his career as academician, Zhuo drafted an edict that Chancellor Sang Weihan altered.
units.literal: At the beginning, when Zhuo was an academician, he once drafted an edict that was altered by the chancellor Sang Weihan.

units.zh: 棁以唐故事學士草制有所改者當罷職，乃引經據爭之，維翰頗不樂。
units.en: Zhuo cited Tang precedent that an academician whose draft was altered should leave office, and argued the point from the classics. Weihan was deeply displeased.
units.literal: Zhuo held that by Tang precedent, when an academician's draft edict was altered he ought to be removed from office; he therefore cited the classics and debated on evidence. Weihan was quite displeased.

units.zh: 而棁少專於文學，不能蒞事，維翰乃命棁知貢舉，棁果不能舉職。
units.en: Zhuo had specialized in literature since youth and could not manage affairs. Weihan therefore assigned him charge of the examination, and Zhuo proved unable to perform the duty.
units.literal: Yet Zhuo from youth specialized in literature and could not attend to affairs; Weihan thereupon ordered Zhuo to take charge of the examination, and Zhuo indeed could not fulfill the duty.

units.zh: 時有進士孔英者，素有醜行，為當時所惡。
units.en: There was a jinshi named Kong Ying who had long been notorious for disgraceful conduct and was widely detested.
units.literal: At that time there was a jinshi degree-holder named Kong Ying who had long had disgraceful conduct and was detested by people of the time.

units.zh: 棁既受命，往見維翰，維翰素貴，嚴尊而語簡，謂棁曰：「孔英來矣。」
units.en: After receiving his commission Zhuo went to see Weihan, who was always honored, stern, and brief in speech. He told Zhuo: "Kong Ying has come."
units.literal: After Zhuo received his commission he went to see Weihan. Weihan had always been eminent, stern and dignified with brief speech, and said to Zhuo, "Kong Ying has come.

units.zh: 棁不諭其意，以謂維翰以孔英為言，乃考英及第，物議大以為非，即罷學幹，拜尚書左丞，遷太常卿。
units.en: Zhuo misunderstood and thought Weihan meant to warn him against Kong Ying. He passed Ying in the examination instead, to widespread outrage. Zhuo was removed from the Hanlin Academy, made left assistant director in the Ministry of State Affairs, and transferred to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: Zhuo did not understand his meaning and supposed Weihan was speaking of Kong Ying; he therefore examined Ying and passed him. Public discussion greatly regarded this as wrong. [Zhuo] was immediately removed from the Hanlin Academy, appointed Left Assistant Director in the Ministry of State Affairs, and transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 五年，高祖詔太常復文武二舞，詳定正、冬朝會禮及樂章。
units.en: In the fifth year Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix the rites of the regular and winter court assemblies and their musical pieces.
units.literal: In the fifth year, Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances, and to fix in detail the rites of the regular and winter court assemblies and their musical pieces.

units.zh: 自唐末之亂，禮樂制度亡失已久，棁與御史中丞竇貞固、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允等草定之。
units.en: Ritual and music had been lost since the chaos at the end of Tang. Zhuo worked with Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister Lü Qi, Vice Minister Zhang Yun, and others to draft the regulations.
